correctness.rationale: A compact convex polygon admits a unique area-bisecting offset for each line normal because clipped area is strictly increasing through the supporting interval. Dihedral symmetry reduces normals to one sector 0<=phi<=delta. The proof establishes the two support intersection edges remain the same reflected pair throughout that entire sector (including triangular n=3). Subtracting the fixed polygonal cap from the wedge gives constant area of a triangle with endpoint ray distances a,b from the common reflected vertex, so ab is constant. Express a/b=exp(2s); elementary direction trigonometry gives tan(phi)=cot(delta)*tanh(s) (with sign absorbed by orientation) and the cosine rule yields the displayed L(phi). Strict increase with |phi| follows from positive tan(delta), giving exact min/max and endpoint equality cases. Direct independent polygon clipping/binary search of the half-area offset, entirely separate from the analytic formula, agreed for each of n=3,5,7,9,17,31 at seven normal angles per sector with max error 9e-16. Taylor expansion gives difference R*pi^2/(4n^2). Finite confirmation alone is not a universal proof; sector containment and wedge-area geometry are the universal arguments.
